cultural.vision_reason: This is a leather horse-harness rein with plaited straps, dyed-leather decoration, and amulet-like triangular elements—consistent with Hausa leatherwork traditions of equestrian gear made for horse-riding elites in the Sahel/Niger region. The item is plausible for the claimed people and region.

physical.title: rein; horse-harness
physical.summary: Pair of reins for horse. Composed of single plaited leather strap which divides into three plaited straps bound at intervals with light green-dyed leather. Further division into two separate bunches of three plaited leather straps which form the bridle and terminate in leather loops for attachment of bit. Immediately before loops, leather straps are bound together with light green-dyed leather. Four triangular decorative elements are attached at top and bottom, made of leather pieces glued and sewn together. Two largest amulets on each side of bridle are backed with red-dyed leather pieces with black linear tooling as well as yellow-dyed leather pieces with lines of green ink decoration. Front is covered with light green-dyed leather with applied red wool disks with spoke pattern in strips of blue, green and yellow cotton cloth, cut out sections, inserts of black cotton cloth and narrow bands of multicoloured dyed leather. Black cotton thread stitched in linear patterns. Smaller four triangular pieces are of similar composition but decorated on green dyed leather with cut outs filled with red wool cloth and black linear stitching.
